headline_marked: Papers sent to Dubai to [[extradite former IGP Benazir Ahmed]]
headline: Papers sent to Dubai to extradite former IGP Benazir Ahmed
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmad says the government sent the necessary documents within three days of the request, despite a 30-day window.
details: Bangladesh has officially requested the extradition of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed from Dubai. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmad confirmed that the necessary paperwork was dispatched via diplomatic channels within three days of the request.

The Home Minister revealed that while Dubai had provided a 30-day window to submit the documents, the government acted swiftly, translating approximately 144 pages of documentation into Arabic before sending them.
Benazir Ahmed served as the IGP and Director General of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) under the previous Awami League government. His arrest in Dubai was first disclosed in parliament on June 14.

The government stated it will continue to press for his return, acknowledging that Dubai has its own legal processes to follow. Bangladesh has previously successfully exchanged detainees with Dubai through Mutual Legal Assistance Requests under the UN Charter.
Separately, the Home Minister noted that police nationwide are on high alert to maintain security and prevent instability, particularly around the founding anniversary of the Awami League.
caption:
Bangladesh has moved to bring back former IGP Benazir Ahmed from Dubai, submitting extradition papers in just three days.

Bangladesh has officially requested the extradition of former Inspector General of Police (IGP) Benazir Ahmed from Dubai. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmad confirmed that the necessary paperwork was dispatched via diplomatic channels within three days of the request.

The Home Minister revealed that while Dubai had provided a 30-day window to submit the documents, the government acted swiftly, translating approximately 144 pages of documentation into Arabic before sending them.

Benazir Ahmed served as the IGP and Director General of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) under the previous Awami League government. His arrest in Dubai was first disclosed in parliament on June 14.

The government stated it will continue to press for his return, acknowledging that Dubai has its own legal processes to follow. Bangladesh has previously successfully exchanged detainees with Dubai through Mutual Legal Assistance Requests under the UN Charter.

Separately, the Home Minister noted that police nationwide are on high alert to maintain security and prevent instability, particularly around the founding anniversary of the Awami League.

headline_marked: Teesta River [[nears danger level]] as rising waters threaten northern districts
headline: Teesta River nears danger level as rising waters threaten northern districts
summary: Water levels at the Teesta Barrage point are just 13cm below the danger mark, raising fears of flooding in five districts.
details: The water level of the Teesta River has risen sharply due to continuous rainfall and upstream runoff from the hills, threatening five northern districts with flooding.

According to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), the water level at the Teesta Barrage point in Lalmonirhat was 52.02 metres at 9:00am today, just 13 centimetres below the danger level of 52.15 metres.
BWDB officials warn that the river may cross the danger mark at any time, potentially triggering widespread flooding across the Teesta basin.
Low-lying settlements and char areas have already begun to go under water, inundating homes and agricultural land in several places.
Farmers in Hatibandha and Kaliganj upazilas report that their homes and Aman paddy seedbeds have already been submerged.
The districts most at risk include Lalmonirhat, Kurigram, Nilphamari, Rangpur, and Gaibandha.
While the Teesta is rising rapidly, the Brahmaputra, Dudhkumar, and Dharla rivers in Kurigram currently remain below their respective danger levels.
BWDB officials are closely monitoring the situation and report that increased water flow has also caused riverbank erosion at several points along the Teesta.
